memo.verdict: Park. Neutral; not yet investable; conviction medium that it is not yet investable, low on the direction of the next print. The record does not invalidate: it names a price and a date at which the case re-opens. Re-open at about SEK 15.5 (just below the 52-week low of SEK 15.54), where the probability-weighted path clears the 20 percent bar, or on the Q3 2026 report of 12 November 2026 if it shows Norway profitable, Clear Line above 30 percent and the SEK 1,250 million bond priced inside 8 percent, whichever comes first. The park rule applies on three of its four gates (management D, business quality D, predictability D; trackability C) and the record does not argue otherwise. The thesis in the record's words: Fasadgruppen is a major-cause-for-concern case in which the concern has been addressed on the balance sheet and in the leadership but not yet in the operations; at SEK 16.5 the shares pay 4.4 times the consensus earnings two years forward, which is the price of the branch in which the recovery does not come; what the price does not pay for is the legacy Nordic business returning to a 6 percent margin while Clear Line holds 25 percent, and that recovery has one quarter of evidence behind it. The bet, when the price or the print allows it, is that an operator-led, recapitalised Fasadgruppen returns its legacy Nordic business to a 6 percent margin while Clear Line holds 25 percent, and that the market then pays 7.5 times the earnings two years forward. The drop-through sensitivity names the condition under which the recommendation turns bearish: a bond at 9 percent, the SEK 806 million of acquisition liabilities refinanced with debt at 7 percent and a 25 percent tax rate take FY2028 earnings per share from SEK 3.20 to about SEK 2.28 and the eighteen-month return to about nil, at which the 'Modal return' would be F, the 'Investment Thesis' D and the recommendation bearish rather than park.
case: The thesis. A major-cause-for-concern case addressed on the balance sheet and in the leadership but not yet in the operations; at SEK 16.5, 4.4 times consensus earnings two years forward, the price is that of the branch in which the recovery does not come; unpriced is the legacy Nordic business back to 6 percent while Clear Line holds 25 percent, which has one quarter of evidence.

The change is a repair, carried out inside twelve months, and real. The roll-up ran leverage to 5.3 times buying Clear Line for up to SEK 2.2 billion in late 2024, then met a Nordic construction downturn, a record-cold Q1 2026 and a UK regulator taking about 36 weeks against a statutory eight. Since then: recapitalised (SEK 504 million rights issue, April 2026), pruned (Alnova, December 2025), flattened (one management layer removed, February 2025, credited with lifting the adjusted EBITA margin from 5.7 percent in 2024 to 8.2 percent in 2025), re-led (acting chief executive 21 August 2026; permanent finance director 5 October 2026). Each removes a reason the shares were uninvestable in 2025; none adds a reason to own them.

The forces are of ordinary strength and pull both ways, so the change is in magnitude, not force. 'Change Forces' (E 1, BB 1) C. 'External forces' C: the company's own cycle B (the strongest external force: organic from -11.7 percent in Q1 2026 to -0.5 percent in Q2; record backlog; the weakest comparison base in listed history for H2 2026 and Q1 2027; margin by quarter Q1 2026 0.5 percent against 6.5 percent, Q2 7.6 percent against about 11.5 percent, H2 2025 8.4 percent; not A because the turn is one quarter old and the cohort's lesson is that the market pays for the organic volume print); competition D (new-build contractors bidding into Swedish renovation; DNB Carnegie: rising "until the residential new-build market recovers"; Balco's renovation margin 2.3 percent in Q2 2026; 83 percent of exterior-work operators report margin compression; the force most likely to cap the margin recovery); demand C (Swedish starts +8.0 percent July 2026, Byggstartsindikatorn +8.0 percent, non-residential starts +13.2 percent, housing transactions +12 percent, sentiment 102.9; EPBD transposition deadline of 29 May 2026 missed by every state, infringement opened 15 July 2026, "a renovation law in infringement is not demand"; UK remediation 14,600 buildings assessed, about 1,400 completed; Norway weak at 4.5 percent policy rate, Finland's renovation market down a third year, UK starts 18 percent below prior year); political and regulatory C (ROT reverted from 50 to 30 percent in 2026, a headwind; Villaeffekten from 1 September 2026, 30 percent of eligible material costs up to SEK 60,000 per small house, SEK 300 million a year through 2030, partial exposure because the company's Swedish customers are associations about 25 percent of group revenue, public sector about 25 percent, commercial owners; BSR action plan to 12 weeks by December 2026, given even odds at best; four approvals worth GBP 32.5 million in December 2025); supply side D (Saint-Gobain insulation +35 percent, Kingspan +31 to 37 percent; materials 50.57 percent of H1 2026 net sales, SEK 1,215.9 million; contracts fixed-price, indexation "rarely" offsets, overruns absorbed up to 10 percent; Swedish agreed minimum wages +8 percent for 2027 on a cost base 40 to 50 percent labour; offsets central procurement across about 70 subsidiaries); macro D (Riksbank expected to hike 25 basis points in November 2026 toward 2.50 percent by mid-2027; Norges Bank 4.5 percent; sensitivities: a 2.0 percentage-point organic volume drop lowers earnings per share 11.5 percent, a 50 basis-point margin swing 11.1 percent; not F because Swedish data improve despite rates and the Swedish country tilt is Overweight); currency catch-all C (non-SEK revenue 53.85 percent of 2025 sales; a 5 percent adverse move costs about SEK 12.2 million of EBITA on 2024 levels or SEK 17.2 million on 2025 asset levels, SEK 0.11 of earnings per share; consensus path SEK appreciation, EUR/SEK 10.40 to 10.60 by end-2027; NOK 17 percent of sales); disruption C (prefabrication, robotics, lightweight materials at the margin; bespoke restoration insulates). 'Internal forces' C: broad (chief executive, finance director, deputy chair, structure, perimeter, capital structure, bid discipline, acquisition filter) but no single strong force; screen flags 'caretaker chief executive' and 'dangerous leverage' present in the last twelve months and only partly cleared. Balance sheet C (the largest internal force, running the other way: utilisation reduced; the bond is the one utilisation ahead, at an unknown coupon in a week when European credit saw one of its sharpest weekly falls since 2000; loaded claims about SEK 2,420 million against about SEK 1,442 million of market capitalisation; not B because a repair, not an enabler); chief executive C (the right direction, an operator, but an acting vacancy; "transitionally uncertain but operationally credible"; SB1 Markets: the departure "increases recovery uncertainty"); standards B (the February 2025 flattening; bid duality; declining low-margin work; central savings SEK 10 to 20 million a year; Norway leadership; hurdle-share plan, maximum dilution 0.76 percent; not A because one year of evidence whose second half was the worst first half on margin); strategy C (articulated from deleveraging to "profitable growth", volume to margin, cash-funded niche acquisitions; the 2028 targets kept, implying 22 percent compound growth, "virtually unachievable without dilutive equity or increased debt"; Inderes models SEK 5.99 billion for 2028 without acquisitions); guidance F (none to raise); other leaders C (finance director, deputy chair, founder as Chairman, board shareholding policy, Norway leadership; no activist above 3 percent); perimeter C (Alnova, about ten units folded, small against 55 subsidiaries); acquisitions D (halted about twelve months; ProRakenne EUR 5.2 million of revenue, Liab Plåtbyggarna SEK 80 million; FY2025 acquisition cash flow SEK 33.3 million against SEK 736 million in FY2024; impairments; 'empire-building' absent now, present in 2024); price rises F ("muted pricing due to high competition"; contract rates stagnated through inflation; the only pricing power in scope expansion of about 20 percent and Clear Line's niche, 37.7 percent in Q2 2026 from 29.4 percent, "partly driven by timing effects"); shareholder returns F; earnings-quality catch-all D (items affecting comparability SEK 145.2 million in 2025; unreviewed Q2 2026 interim; options SEK 712.9 million and earn-outs SEK 93.3 million inherited); new geographies C (Clear Line already in the numbers; ProRakenne); new products D.
counter_case: The FALSE FRIEND, the risk research's own winning hypothesis, at full force. Fasadgruppen is a volume-chaser whose headline stabilisation (order backlog +6.6 percent organic, Clear Line's 37.7 percent margin in Q2 2026, leverage down to 3.3 times) masks structural decay. Organic growth averaged about 1 percent a year from 2020 to 2025 through a decade of acquisitions and about -5 percent a year in the 2023 to 2025 downturn. The legacy Nordic margin is 5 percent because Swedish tenders are won on price and new-build contractors have moved in; the renovation market is being flooded by contractors bidding for volume. Cash conversion fell to 26.3 percent in H1 2026 from 56.3 percent, against a peer range of 70 to 90 percent. Returns on invested capital were 6 to 7 percent in 2024 and 2025 against SEK 4,066 million of goodwill, and SEK 806 million of acquisition liabilities sit outside the reported net debt above SEK 1,442 million of equity. Clear Line's margin is an outlier that experts expect to normalise. On this reading the multiple is not low, it is right: the 4.4 times has been the market's settled view for two years (two-year median 4.36 times), not a dislocation; the equity is a geared option on a multiple and a margin that both sit at their natural level; and the market has decided that "margin discipline and low leverage get the multiple; volume-chasing gets the discount". The next event is a target reset by a new chief executive followed by a second equity raise. The evidence for this is most of the evidence in the folder, and the record concedes most of the facts and the direction of the competitive evidence: the organic record, the cash conversion, the leverage stack, the competitive direction, the leadership vacancy, and that 4.4 times has been settled for two years.

At 'Foundations' level the counter-case runs the other way and is also conceded on the facts: the company is the Nordic leader in a market growing about 7 percent a year, 80 to 90 percent of revenue is renovation that must be done, customers repeat at 80 to 90 percent, no customer or supplier exceeds 10 percent, the model is asset-light with net working capital of about 1 percent of sales, and the UK business has a regulatory moat earning 30 percent margins; the record's answer is that none of this stopped the organic line falling about 5 percent a year, the margin halving in 2024 to 5.7 percent, or the Swedish subsidiaries being undercut, because these are strengths of market position, not competitive position, and the business research's own largest risk (new-build pivots) has since been evidenced by Balco at 2.3 percent.
triggers: Re-open: the price at or below about SEK 15.5, or the Q3 2026 report on 12 November 2026 showing Norway profitable and Clear Line above 30 percent with the bond priced inside 8 percent, whichever comes first.

The re-rating condition: the group's last-twelve-month adjusted EBITA margin at or above 8.0 percent at June 2027 (the record's path 7.8 percent); the margin series itself, quarter by quarter, is what would change the odds (35 percent at eighteen months, 50 percent at three years).

The legacy Nordic margin: up if the Q3 2026 group adjusted EBITA margin is at or above 9 percent with Norway described as profitable; down if Q3 is below 9 percent or Q4 2026 misses the usual cash release; invalidate on a FY2027 group margin below 7.0 percent or a legacy margin below 5 percent in FY2027.

Clear Line and the BSR: up on two consecutive quarters above 30 percent (the research's own test); down on a quarter below 25 percent or UK sales down year on year in Q4 2026; invalidate on two consecutive quarters below 20 percent; the BSR's December 2026 deadline for 12-week decisions, given even odds at best; the BSR's published Gateway 2 durations as the primary leading operational indicator.

The balance sheet: up on a bond priced inside 8 percent at full size; down on a size cut, a coupon above 9 percent or a covenant waiver request; leverage below 3.0 times at December 2026 probable (the record's path 2.9 times), below 2.5 times by Q2 2027 possible only (about 35 percent); the settlement of SEK 712.9 million of options and SEK 93.3 million of earn-outs, with undisclosed payout triggers; a second equity raise invalidates.

The leadership: a permanent chief executive within six months probable (about 65 percent); an appointee without operating experience, down; a reset of the 2028 targets with building blocks, up (and the missing 'guidance rebased' condition supplied); no appointment by the FY2026 report is the alarm.
